solutions.check: 30 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Poor quality budget presented by Straw?

parts.note: budget as an adjective means low-cost
Jack Straw, the Labour Home and Foreign Secretary

explanation.surface: A cut-price budget announced by Jack Straw is mocked as shoddy.
explanation.walkthrough: Straw was never Chancellor, so the surface jeers at an imagined budget; the name splits off as the first name of the politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheapjack is an adjective for shoddy, inferior goods, like those sold by a hawker of cheap wares.

clue.text: Stink from backside of game

indicators.note: the backside is the rear half, so only the back portion of the game's name is kept

parts.note: ping-pong, another name for table tennis

explanation.surface: A bad smell wafting from someone's rear during a game.
explanation.walkthrough: Ping-pong drops its front half, PING, leaving the back half.
explanation.definitionFit: Pong is British slang for a strong unpleasant smell, a synonym of stink.

clue.text: Give him time? No, sir — Brown is only 50% backed

indicators.note: backed means put into reverse, so the whole string is read from the end

parts.note: taken as written
Gordon Brown was Prime Minister

indicators.note: only half of the little word is kept, here its first of two letters

parts.note: the first half of the two-letter word

explanation.surface: Someone pleads against jailing a man while sniping that Brown has only half-hearted backing.
explanation.walkthrough: NOSIR + PM + I read backwards gives I-MP-RIS-ON.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone time is to sentence them to a prison term, so it means to jail them.

clue.text: Old ruler wheels round, sea sick

indicators.note: round says the vehicle goes around the other letters, holding them inside

parts.note: wheels is slang for a car

indicators.note: something sick is out of order, so its letters are churned up

parts.note: taken as written before being rearranged

explanation.surface: An ancient ruler turns his chariot about, queasy from the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Caesar was the title of the ancient Roman emperors, rulers of long ago.

clue.text: (& 24dn.) Former colony's view of the English MP, Owen Higgins: corrupted

definitions.text: Former colony's view of the English

indicators.note: corrupted means spoilt and twisted, so the letters of the name are scrambled

parts.note: the letters of the MP's title and the invented name

explanation.surface: A satirical aside about a supposedly corrupt English MP and how a former colony sees him.
explanation.walkthrough: Australians call the English Poms and stereotype them as constant complainers.
explanation.definitionFit: Whingeing Poms is the stock Australian put-down of English immigrants as grumblers, Australia being a former colony.

clue.text: Writing a novel, say, with Archer's effortless ease, being a wanker?

definitions.text: Writing a novel, say, with Archer's effortless ease
definitions.meaning: first meaning: producing something quickly and carelessly, as Jeffrey Archer churns out novels
second meaning: British slang for masturbating

explanation.walkthrough: Jeffrey Archer is a Tory peer and bestselling novelist; the vulgar second sense is typical Private Eye.
explanation.definitionFit: To toss something off is to produce it with little effort; the same phrase is crude slang for self-gratification.

clue.text: Pornographic, dual controlled model?

indicators.note: controlled means handled and steered about, so the letters are moved into a new order

parts.note: taken as written before being rearranged
the Model T, Ford's famous early car

explanation.surface: A question about a dual-control model with a smutty undertone.
explanation.definitionFit: Adult used of films or magazines is a euphemism for sexually explicit material.

clue.text: Breaking mould after House makes you a crook

parts.note: HO is the standard abbreviation for house

indicators.note: breaking a cast shatters it, so its letters are reassembled differently

parts.note: taken as written before being rearranged

explanation.surface: Breaking the mould once you are in the House turns a politician into a criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after House' places the scrambled letters behind HO.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoodlum is a thug or gangster, a type of criminal or crook.

clue.text: see 27dn.
Has screwed a banger, not far from Dover

indicators.note: screwed means twisted round, so the word's letters are turned into a new order

parts.note: taken as written before being rearranged
a banger is British slang for an old car, here a Ford

explanation.surface: Someone has had sex in an old car somewhere near Dover.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes a place rather than naming it: a town in Kent within easy reach of the port of Dover.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashford is a Kent town about twenty miles from the Channel port of Dover, so it is a place near it.

clue.text: CIA's pissed with Al Gore dropping round for Spanish port

indicators.note: pissed is British slang for drunk, so the letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe ignored
taken as written

indicators.note: dropping means the round letter falls out of Gore

parts.note: taken as written, minus its O
a round thing is shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: American spies get drunk with the former US vice-president.
explanation.walkthrough: Gore dropping O leaves GRE; CIAS, AL and GRE are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: Algeciras is a port city in southern Spain, across the bay from Gibraltar.

clue.text: US body sending people up, connected with length of organ

parts.note: the American space agency, which launches astronauts
L is the abbreviation for length

explanation.surface: An American body mocking people, linked to the length of a man's organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sending people up' suggests satire but means rocket launches; the organ is the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasal means relating to the nose, the organ of smell.

clue.text: (& 15ac.) Demoted Thatcher follower becomes dancing star

indicators.note: demoted means the military rank in the name is replaced by a lower one

parts.note: John Major succeeded Margaret Thatcher as Prime Minister

explanation.surface: A downgraded successor to Thatcher turns into a celebrity on the dance floor.
explanation.walkthrough: A major outranks a sergeant, so demoting John Major gives the name. John Sergeant, a political journalist, was a famous contestant on Strictly Come Dancing, a BBC dance show.
explanation.definitionFit: The journalist became a celebrated contestant on the BBC ballroom competition in 2008.

clue.text: MPs assembled with slits in trousers — they love filth

parts.note: the House of Commons, where MPs gather
flies are the front openings of trousers

explanation.surface: Members of Parliament gather with their trouser flies undone, and they relish smut.
explanation.definitionFit: Houseflies are insects drawn to rubbish and dung, creatures that thrive on dirt.

clue.text: see 13ac.
Top legislators pissed with Brenda's entourage?

parts.note: high as in intoxicated
Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for the Queen, whose attendants form her court

explanation.surface: Senior lawmakers are drunk alongside the Queen's retinue.
explanation.walkthrough: Brenda is Private Eye's long-running name for Queen Elizabeth II.
explanation.definitionFit: The High Court is a senior court of England and Wales whose judges make law through rulings.

clue.text: What expenses claims represent for the MP, pisspoor yes-man Yeo?

definitions.text: What expenses claims represent for the MP

indicators.note: pisspoor means badly done, so the letters come out in a botched order

parts.note: taken as written; Tim Yeo was a Conservative MP

explanation.surface: A jibe at a Tory MP's expenses, written in the 2009 scandal's spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy money is cash gained with little effort, which is how padded expense claims served MPs.

clue.text: Act like a copper deviously out to secure one in jail

indicators.note: in places the whole secured group inside the word for jail

parts.note: can is slang for prison

indicators.note: to secure is to hold fast, so the rearranged letters hold the one inside them
deviously means by a crooked route, so the letters of out are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A police officer, being sneaky, sets out to lock someone up in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as a description, not a word: a British officer cautions a suspect. 'Out' is not a deletion signal here; it is the material that 'deviously' reorders.
explanation.definitionFit: Police in Britain caution a suspect, formally warning them of their rights, so to caution is a copper's act.

clue.text: Love Hillary's middle being in gonad-busting car

indicators.note: being in says these letters go inside the rearranged word
busting means breaking open, so the word's letters are broken up and reset

parts.note: taken as written before being rearranged
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

indicators.note: the middle of the name is its central letter, the only one kept

parts.note: the central letter of the seven-letter name

explanation.surface: A crude image of Hillary Clinton in a vehicle, kicking someone in the groin.
explanation.definitionFit: A gondola is the passenger car of a cable car, ski lift or airship.

clue.text: Archer at one time converted by "god" Blair

indicators.note: converted means turned into something else, so the letters take a new form

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Jeffrey Archer was once won over to religion by a godlike Tony Blair.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeffrey Archer served time in prison for perjury, and Blair's religious faith was a running Private Eye joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaolbird is someone who has been in prison, which Lord Archer was after his perjury conviction.

clue.text: Little devil interrupts rendition of poem with casual shit

indicators.note: interrupting breaks into the middle, so one set of letters goes inside the other
a rendition is a fresh version, so the word's letters are set out anew

parts.note: taken as written before being rearranged

indicators.note: casual means relaxed and haphazard, so the vulgar word's letters are loosely rearranged

parts.note: taken as written before being rearranged

explanation.surface: A cheeky imp breaks into a poetry reading with offhand swearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little' signals a shortened name: Mephisto is the short form of Mephistopheles.
explanation.definitionFit: Mephisto is a pet short form of Mephistopheles, the devil of the Faust legend.

clue.text: Heavens! After fourth of claims by politician is in, it's next to nothing!

definitions.note: a phrase; skimpy describes something that is barely anything

indicators.note: is in places the letters inside the word for heavens

parts.note: the sky is the heavens

indicators.note: fourth of picks out the letter in the fourth position of the word

parts.note: the fourth letter of the word
Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Good heavens: once a politician's expense claims are in, there is almost nothing left.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a phrase standing for a description: something skimpy is next to nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Skimpy means meagre or scanty, so a skimpy thing amounts to very little.

clue.text: Dodgy erection saint eliminated

indicators.note: eliminated means removed, so the abbreviation is cut out of the slang word

parts.note: a stiffy is slang for an erection
ST is the abbreviation for saint, the part removed

explanation.surface: A questionable building put up after a saint's shrine was demolished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Erection' looks like a building, but it is the vulgar sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Iffy is informal for doubtful or suspect, a synonym of dodgy.

clue.text: Balls familiarly having twitch, front to rear regulation

parts.note: Ed Balls, the Labour minister, by his familiar first name

indicators.note: front to rear says the leading letter is moved round to the end

parts.note: a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: A rule about someone's twitching testicles, crudely put.
explanation.walkthrough: Ed Balls was a Labour Cabinet minister; TIC loses its front letter to the back to become ICT.
explanation.definitionFit: An edict is an official order or decree, a kind of regulation.

clue.text: see 5dn.
Back-to-front cap on party substitute member

indicators.note: back-to-front means the head covering's word is read from its end

parts.note: a lid caps a container
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A partygoer wears his cap backwards and stands in for a club member.
explanation.definitionFit: A dildo is a sex toy used in place of a penis, slangily called a member.

clue.text: How the PM introduces himself on dropping 40%: "I log off — bit of a problem"

indicators.note: dropping 40% loses two of the five letters of the surname, the last two

parts.note: Gordon Brown, a former UK Prime Minister, would say I'm Brown

indicators.note: off means gone bad, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A prime minister signs off a message mid-crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: Gordon Brown was a UK Prime Minister: I'M BROWN with 40% of BROWN gone gives IMBRO; then 'off' rearranges I LOG into GLIO.
explanation.definitionFit: An imbroglio is a confused, embarrassing situation, a tangle or mess, so a bit of a problem.

clue.text: (& 9dn.) Fortune made by wife of knight of the realm, topless Yank

parts.words: wife of knight of the realm
parts.note: the wife of a knight is styled Lady

indicators.note: topless means the first letter is removed

parts.note: to yank is to pluck, pull sharply

explanation.surface: A knight's wife made her fortune; an American lost her top.
explanation.walkthrough: LADY, then PLUCK without its first letter gives LUCK; the answer runs on into 9 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady Luck is the personification of chance, so the phrase stands for fortune.

clue.text: Holder is penetrated by male, er, to become more gay

indicators.note: penetrated means entered, so the other letters go inside the holder's word

parts.note: a cup holds liquid
he is the male pronoun
taken as written

explanation.surface: A smutty remark about a man, er, being turned more homosexual.
explanation.walkthrough: Gay is in its older sense of merry.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheer up is to become happier, matching gay in its old meaning of merry.

clue.text: Re-emerged novelist: career to bite the dust

parts.note: to career is to rush headlong
to bite the dust is to die

explanation.surface: A novelist resurfaces only for his career to crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Career' looks like a noun but is the verb meaning to rush.
explanation.definitionFit: Salman Rushdie came back into public life after years hiding under the fatwa for The Satanic Verses.
